---
title: "Survival models"
subtitle: "Effects on the probability of the event by a chosen time"
---

After `streg`, the marginal effects are changes in the predicted median
survival time by default (the mean after `mestreg`). Predicted survival times
extrapolate beyond the observed follow-up when spells are censored, and Jones
and Metzger (2019) and Metzger and Jones (2022) recommend interpreting
duration models through the probability of the event by a chosen time instead.
With `time(#)`, the marginal effects of `stcox` and `streg` models are changes
in the probability that the event has happened by time *#*, one minus the
survival probability. A Cox model (`stcox`) needs `time()`.

The examples use Stata's `cancer` data: 48 patients in a drug trial, followed
for up to 39 months. `died` records a death, and `drug` is the placebo or one
of two drugs, Other and NA.

```{.stata-run}
. sysuse cancer, clear
(Patient survival in drug trial)

. stset studytime, failure(died)

Survival-time data settings

         Failure event: died!=0 & died<.
Observed time interval: (0, studytime]
     Exit on or before: failure

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
         48  total observations
          0  exclusions
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
         48  observations remaining, representing
         31  failures in single-record/single-failure data
        744  total analysis time at risk and under observation
                                                At risk from t =         0
                                     Earliest observed entry t =         0
                                          Last observed exit t =        39

```

## A Cox model and a Weibull model

The effects of the drugs and of age on the probability of death by month 10,
in a Cox model and a Weibull model:

```{.stata-run}
. quietly stcox age i.drug, vce(robust)

. estimates store cox1

. quietly streg age i.drug, distribution(weibull) vce(robust)

. estimates store wei1

. 
. mecompare drug age, models(cox1 wei1) time(10)

Predicting: Pr(event by t=10)
Marginal effects and cross-model differences (N_cox1=48) (N_wei1=48)

                                 |  ME #   Estimate  Robust SE      P>|z|
---------------------------------+---------------------------------------
drug                             |                                       
             Other - Placebo     |                                       
                            cox1 |     1     -0.419      0.089      0.000
                            wei1 |     2     -0.439      0.093      0.000
                      Difference |     3      0.020      0.032      0.528
                NA - Placebo     |                                       
                            cox1 |     4     -0.538      0.081      0.000
                            wei1 |     5     -0.531      0.085      0.000
                      Difference |     6     -0.007      0.050      0.894
---------------------------------+---------------------------------------
age + 1 (centered)               |                                       
                            cox1 |     7      0.021      0.004      0.000
                            wei1 |     8      0.023      0.005      0.000
                      Difference |     9     -0.002      0.002      0.234

NOTE: the stcox and streg rows are changes in the probability that the event has happened by time 10
> . See mecompare##survival.

```

Compared with the placebo, the Other drug lowers the probability of death by
month 10 by 0.42 in the Cox model and by 0.44 in the Weibull model; the two
models do not differ significantly (Difference 0.020, p = .528).

## A Cox model and a logit

Other models in `models()` keep their default prediction. A logit of whether a
patient died during the study can be compared with the Cox model, here at
month 20:

```{.stata-run}
. quietly logit died age i.drug, vce(robust)

. estimates store lg1

. 
. mecompare drug, models(lg1 cox1) time(20)

Predicting: Pr(died) (lg1), Pr(event by t=20) (cox1)
Marginal effects and cross-model differences (N_lg1=48) (N_cox1=48)

                                 |  ME #   Estimate  Robust SE      P>|z|
---------------------------------+---------------------------------------
drug                             |                                       
             Other - Placebo     |                                       
                             lg1 |     1     -0.551      0.139      0.000
                            cox1 |     2     -0.484      0.096      0.000
                      Difference |     3     -0.066      0.108      0.537
                NA - Placebo     |                                       
                             lg1 |     4     -0.484      0.136      0.000
                            cox1 |     5     -0.719      0.092      0.000
                      Difference |     6      0.235      0.127      0.065

NOTE: the stcox rows are changes in the probability that the event has happened by time 20. See meco
> mpare##survival.

```

The logit's rows are changes in the probability of dying during the study, and
the Cox model's in the probability of dying by month 20. The logit counts every
patient alive at their last follow-up as a survivor, however short their
follow-up; the Cox model takes each patient's follow-up time into account.

## Choosing the time

The time is in the units of the analysis time set by `stset`, here months.
With a Cox model, a time later than the last analysis time, or earlier than the
first event, is refused.

## References

> Song: Advice for Substantively Interpreting Duration Models." *PS: Political
> Science & Politics* 52(4): 691--695.
> <https://doi.org/10.1017/S104909651900060X>

> Metzger, Shawna K., and Benjamin T. Jones. 2022. "Getting Time Right: Using
> Cox Models and Probabilities to Interpret Binary Panel Data." *Political
> Analysis* 30(2): 151--166. <https://doi.org/10.1017/pan.2021.14>
